title: Hybrid Heaven
subtitle: Konami · Nintendo 64
summary: Hybrid Heaven is Konami's Nintendo 64 science-fiction adventure about a conspiracy involving synthetic humans and a hidden installation beneath Manhattan. Exploration uses a directly controlled character who can move, climb and solve obstacles, while encounters with biological weapons introduce a separate combat system. The mixture gives the underground complex two rhythms. A route through its machinery asks for immediate navigation, but meeting an enemy turns attention toward positioning, stored energy and a choice of techniques whose usefulness grows through repeated practice.
body: Hybrid Heaven is Konami's Nintendo 64 science-fiction adventure about a conspiracy involving synthetic humans and a hidden installation beneath Manhattan. Exploration uses a directly controlled character who can move, climb and solve obstacles, while encounters with biological weapons introduce a separate combat system. The mixture gives the underground complex two rhythms. A route through its machinery asks for immediate navigation, but meeting an enemy turns attention toward positioning, stored energy and a choice of techniques whose usefulness grows through repeated practice.

During combat, the character and opponent move around a restricted area in real time. Once an attack is selected, the action pauses for choices and their resolution before movement resumes. Energy can be saved for combinations, making the decision to strike now part of preparing a larger sequence. Attacks and defensive actions develop through use, with separate statistics for different body parts. The fighter's capabilities therefore reflect the techniques being practised, while injuries can make a preferred approach less reliable in the next exchange.

The progression system gives punches, kicks and defensive responses the attention that another role-playing game might reserve for a collection of weapons. Improving a particular part of the body changes the options available when the next creature approaches. Released in 1999, the game also offered an unusual widescreen display option for the console. Its hybrid design is most interesting where the two forms meet: the person exploring the facility is also a developing fighter, with each encounter adding another small decision about the kind of body and technique the player wants to build.
story_headings: An infiltration with another kind of fight
Move into position, then choose the technique
A body becomes the role-playing equipment
